---
title: "Lab 01 — Causal questions and description"
output: learnr::tutorial
runtime: shiny_prerendered
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(learnr)
library(tidyverse)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("lab_submission.R")
resume <- read_csv("data/resume.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
lab_meta <- list(id = "lab01", title = "Causal questions and description")
lab_prompts <- c(
  q1 = "Which question is a causal question?",
  q2 = "The callback gap (White-sounding names minus Black-sounding names) is about…",
  q3 = "The mean of call equals…",
  q4 = "Why can we not read the effect for one particular résumé off this file?"
)
```

## What you will do

Separate a description from an effect question, then summarise the callback indicator. Download the `.txt` and upload it.

```{r means, exercise=TRUE, exercise.lines=6}
resume %>%
  group_by(race) %>%
  summarise(callback = mean(call), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r q1}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q1"]],
  answer("What is the effect of a Black-sounding name on the callback rate?", correct = TRUE),
  answer("What is the callback rate in this file?"),
  answer("How many résumés are in the file?"),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q2}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q2"]],
  answer("3 percentage points (about 9.6 percent versus 6.4 percent).", correct = TRUE),
  answer("30 percentage points."),
  answer("Zero. The résumés were identical, so the rates match."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q3}
question(
  lab_prompts[["q3"]],
  answer("The callback rate, because call is 0 or 1.", correct = TRUE),
  answer("The median name."),
  answer("The causal effect for every résumé."),
  allow_retry = TRUE,
  random_answer_order = TRUE
)
```

```{r q4}
question_text(
  lab_prompts[["q4"]],
  open_answer(),
  placeholder = "One résumé, one name, and the missing counterfactual.",
  trim = TRUE
)
```


## Submit

Type your name, download the text file, and upload it. Submit the questions first so the file contains your answers.

```{r submit-ui, echo=FALSE}
shiny::textInput("student_name", "Your name", placeholder = "Name Surname")
shiny::downloadButton("download_txt", "Download submission .txt")
```

```{r submit-server, context="server"}
output$download_txt <- shiny::downloadHandler(
  filename = function() lab_submission_filename(input$student_name, lab_meta$id),
  content = function(file) {
    write_lab_submission(
      path = file,
      name = input$student_name,
      lab_id = lab_meta$id,
      lab_title = lab_meta$title,
      state = shiny::reactiveValuesToList(learnr::get_tutorial_state()),
      prompts = lab_prompts
    )
  }
)
```
